title: The Triplet's Country Home Murder Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Sonoko) omitted by convention. No event nodes: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved, sharing an order integer. Two genuine red herrings: witness Ayako Suzuki mistakenly names Yuzo as the killer, having glimpsed only the culprit's eyes and nose in a lightning flash and not knowing he has two identical triplet brothers; and Tatsuji is caught in a real lie about his whereabouts (claiming an Okinawa business trip when he'd actually secretly gone to see his ailing fiancee in Tokyo) that is unrelated to the murder. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Taichi's original claimed alibi -- listening to the game at an Osaka pachinko parlor past 11:30 PM -- is impossible, since pachinko parlors are legally required to close by 11:00 PM.

The Tomizawa residence's answering machine timestamps Taichi's message at 11:34 PM, squarely inside the 10-minute blackout that struck at 11:30 -- but the machine's recording circuit (unlike its battery-powered clock) cannot function without power, meaning the message could not actually have been recorded at the time it claims.

Taichi describes the game-winning hit as pulled 'to the right,' a detail from watching the television broadcast, when his revised story claims he only heard it on the radio in Osaka -- the mismatch is what starts unraveling his account before the answering-machine proof lands the case.

Tatsuji's claimed Okinawa-to-Haneda flight is shown to have landed after the time he says he arrived, exposing a real lie about his whereabouts -- but it turns out to be an unrelated cover story for secretly visiting his fiancee in Tokyo, not the murder.
